events.summary:
* WHAT...High waves and dangerous currents expected.

* WHERE...Beaches along Lake Michigan in Door, Kewaunee and
Manitowoc Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming conditions are expected. Strong
currents can pull swimmers into deeper water and high waves
can sweep people off piers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Several beaches that will be most
susceptible to the dangerous swimming conditions include...
Rock Island State Beach, Baileys Harbor beaches and Whitefish
Dunes Beach in Door County. Cresent Beach and City of Kewaunee
Beach in Kewaunee County. Point Beach, Neshotah Beach and Red
Arrow Beach in Manitowoc County.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Brunswick County in south central Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 100 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1105 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1.5 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lawrenceville, Dolphin, Edgerton, Prices Mill, Warfield,
Callaville and Meredithville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1000 PM MST.

* At 802 PM MST, the public reported continued flash flooding from
earlier thunderstorms across the warned area. Washes were running
high across the region with flooding impacts to continue into the
late evening. Additional rainfall will mainly be less than 0.25
inches.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sierra Vista, Benson, Willcox, Whetstone, Huachuca City, St. David,
Tombstone, Dragoon, Pearce-Sunsites, Kartchner Caverns State Park,
Fort Huachuca, Cochise, Texas Canyon, Fairbank, Charleston, Kansas
Settlement, Muleshoe Ranch Preserve and Cascabel.

This includes the following highways...
Route 90 between mile markers 290 and 336. Route 80 between mile
markers 293 and 333. Route 191 between mile markers 43 and 66. Route
92 between mile markers 322 and 323. Interstate 10 between mile
markers 299 and 344. Route 82 between mile markers 50 and 67. Route
186 between mile markers 327 and 335.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Davis Rd between HWY 80 & HWY 191.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED IN THE WESTERN
COLUMBIA RIVER GORGE TUESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH WEDNESDAY EVENING
FOR DRY CONDITIONS AND EASTERLY WINDS UP TO 40 MPH...

* AFFECTED AREA...In Washington, Fire Weather Zone 636 Western
Columbia River Gorge in Oregon and Washington.

* WINDS...East 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 40 mph. Winds will be
strongest Tuesday morning through early Tuesday afternoon, and
again Tuesday night through early Wednesday afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-20 percent. Relative humidity
values will be lowest Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday afternoon.
Poor overnight humidity recoveries are expected Tuesday night
with maximum relative humidity values ranging between 35-45%.

* IMPACTS...Conditions may be favorable for rapid fire spread
which may threaten life and property. Use extra caution with
potential ignition sources, especially in grassy areas.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
